subject: DPA Annex: Custodian windows, subprocessor notification & cross-border flow controls
messages:
From: Carlos Alvarez <c.alvarez@aureliacare.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA annex questions: key custody windows & subproc notify

Diego / team,

Thanks for the updated DPA annex you shared in the call earlier — we've been reviewing with our legal and infosec leads. A few items we'd like clarified before we proceed to signature: 

1) Custodian handoff windows: the annex mentions a 48-hour window for key escrow retrieval during incident response. Can you confirm whether that window is measured in calendar hours or business hours, and whether it is the same for on-prem deployments vs VPCs?

2) Subprocessor notification: we need a commitment to 30 days' advance notice for any new subprocessor that will have access to logs or telemetry for private deployments. Can you accept 30 days for both Hosted and Dedicated tiers, and if not, please specify where the carve-outs are.

3) Cross-border data flows: our compliance team flagged the clause that allows operator troubleshooting from non-US locations. We need a clear statement on whether troubleshooting access to customer-controlled keys or plaintext data is permitted, and what controls (breakglass, audit logs, geo-restrictions) Redwood will put in place.

Attached is a marked-up version of the annex and the current subprocessor list. We can jump on a short call if easier.

Thanks,
Carlos
Carlos Alvarez
Head of Security & Privacy
AureliaCare

Attachments: DPA-Annex-v2_comments.pdf (annotations), Subprocessor-Questions.xlsx
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Alvarez <c.alvarez@aureliacare.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA annex questions: key custody windows & subproc notify

Carlos — appreciate the clear notes. Quick answers up front, then I put more detail below and attached a proposed redline (DPA-Annex-v2.pdf):

- Custodian handoff window: calendar hours; 48-hour standard for Hosted and Dedicated. For Private (customer-controlled on-prem/BYO-K), we can offer an extended 72-hour window unless the customer opts into an expedited 24-hour emergency path (requires signed SLA addendum).

- Subprocessor notification: we can commit to 30 days' advance notice for subprocessors that have access to telemetry or logs. For subprocessors that only operate on control-plane metadata (no telemetry/PII), we request a 14-day notification window. We will highlight each subprocessor's access category in the list.

- Cross-border troubleshooting: operator access to customer-controlled keys or plaintext is not permitted. Troubleshooting access will be limited to metadata and aggregated telemetry unless explicit, scoped, and auditable breakglass is approved by the customer's security admin. Breakglass events will trigger immutable audit logs, justify the access, and be subject to post-incident review. Geo-restrictions: we can commit to routing support sessions to US/EU-only operator pools for your account.

I've attached the redline and an updated subprocessor matrix CSV that tags access levels and notice windows. If this aligns, I propose a short call Friday to go over the escrow timing and finalize the SLA addendum language.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: DPA-Annex-v2.pdf, Subprocessor-List-20270605.csv
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 09:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: AureliaCare DPA follow-ups (prep for 6/5 call)

Diego / Irene — drafting internal play before we hop on the call with AureliaCare tomorrow. Notes: 

- Custodian windows: propose we offer 48h calendar hours for Redwood-hosted and dedicated pools; 72h for on-prem where physical handover is needed. Keep the 24h emergency path as a contractual optional addendum that requires customer-signed operational runbook (to avoid accidental entitlements).

- Subproc notice: we should accept 30-day notify for any subproc with telemetry/PII access. For our legal team: ensure we classify each subproc as (a) telemetry-only, (b) control-plane, (c) custodian/key-management. Attach classification to the CSV.

- Geo-restricted support: commit to operator pools in US/EU for AureliaCare, add a bullet in the annex for "default operator geofence" with escape for customer-requested exceptions.

Action items before call: Marcus to confirm operator-pool routing feasibility and provide list of US/EU operator regions. Diego to prepare the redline and the 72h on-prem language. Irene to loop Security for breakglass audit retention duration (propose 7 years).

Naomi
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Alvarez <c.alvarez@aureliacare.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Mandy Lin <mandy.lin@aureliacare.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2027 15:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA annex questions: custodian windows & subproc notify — proposed final language

Carlos / team — thanks for the call today. Per our discussion, attaching the proposed final redline and calling out the key commitments below so legal can pull into the DPA: 

- Custodian handoff:
  • Hosted & Dedicated (Redwood-managed): 48 calendar hours for key material retrieval in non-emergency scenarios.
  • Private BYO-K / On-prem: 72 calendar hours standard; customers may contract an expedited 24-hour emergency retrieval path via SLA addendum (requires signed runbook and pre-authorized access window).

- Subprocessor notification:
  • 30 days' advance notice for any new subprocessor that will have access to logs, telemetry, or any customer-generated content.
  • 14 days' notice for control-plane subprocessors with metadata-only access.
  • Updated subprocessor CSV (attached) includes a per-subprocessor access tag and estimated notice window.

- Operator/support access & cross-border controls:
  • Operator troubleshooting access to customer-controlled keys or plaintext is explicitly prohibited.
  • Breakglass exceptions may be approved by the customer's security admin; each event will generate an immutable audit trail including operator identity, justification, and time-bounded access.
  • For AureliaCare, Redwood will route support sessions to US/EU operator pools by default. Any exception requires explicit written approval.

Next steps: please confirm if the attached redline matches your expectations and whether your counsel needs any additional specificity on audit retention for breakglass (Naomi recommended 7 years; AureliaCare to confirm). If all good, we'll prepare the DPA signature packet and DocuSign link.

Thanks again — appreciated the constructive conversation.

Diego Fernandez
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0198

Attachments: DPA-Annex-v2.pdf (redline), Subprocessor-List-20270605.csv (tagged)
